thread:
Maya: Heads up — p95 jumped for /v1/complete in EU after routing-affinity rollout.
Ravi: Noticed that too. p50 stable, p99 mostly unchanged. p95 up ~120ms.
Leo: Any change to sampling or merge mode? Console rolls up by transport + timezone.
Maya: We flipped routing-affinity to prefer gpu-pool-A for mobile clients around the time it started.
Deckard (deploy-bot): canary deploy routing-affinity v3 -> 10% at 2026-03-18T13:08:22Z :robot_face: 
Ravi: I pulled the console query: `SELECT approx_percentile(latency_ms, 0.95) AS p95, transport, timezone FROM telemetry WHERE endpoint='/v1/complete' GROUP BY transport, timezone` — the transport split looks weird.
Leo: Could be sample_origin mismatch. Console default is `sample_origin=proxy`, routing telemetry tags `sample_origin=gateway`. Merge of different sample sources can skew percentiles.
Maya: Running per-transport p95 now. Quick output: `http p95=240ms (count=18k), grpc p95=110ms (count=6k)`
Ravi: Huh. That explains it. More http traffic hit pool-A. But why p99 didn't move? p99 stayed ~480ms.
Leo: TDigest/approx_percentile merge behavior can affect mid-tail more than extreme tail. If http distribution has a denser mid-tail, p95 moves without p99 shifting much.
Maya: Hypothesis: affinity shifted a larger fraction of moderate-latency http requests to pool-A (slightly higher median), while long-tail requests still route to fallback pools, leaving p99 stable.
Ravi: Can we verify sample counts and origins? `count_by(sample_origin, transport)` shows sample_origin=gateway contributions jumped for http.
Leo: Also remember we switched rollup window to 5m decay in the console during the rollout — decay can amplify short-term p95 jitter.
Maya: UX action: surface per-transport toggle + sample_origin legend on the latency card. Right now it's too implicit.
Deckard (deploy-bot): Filed ENG-1284: "show sample origin & per-transport counts on percentile card" https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/ENG-1284 :white_check_mark:
Leo: Short-term mitigation: add a small widget that shows p50/p95/p99 by transport and a drilldown link with `?sample_origin=all`. I'll add it to the EU /v1/complete dashboard.
Ravi: Also recommend alert change: normalize regression checks by sample count (e.g., require delta && min_samples) so we don't page on low-count shifts.
Maya: Running a controlled rollback of affinity to 0% now to confirm.
Deckard (deploy-bot): canary routing-affinity v3 rolled back to 0% at 2026-03-18T13:42:11Z per @Maya request.
Maya: After rollback p95 back within baseline. Closing hypothesis: routing-affinity + sample-origin mismatch + short decay window caused the p95 blip.
Ravi: Good call. Follow-ups: (1) surface sample_origin in the console, (2) add per-transport pctl toggle, (3) tweak regression alerting to account for sample counts.
Leo: I'll open the PR for the widget and a short docs blurb explaining merge/source provenance for percentiles.
Maya: Thanks all — nice example of how routing policy + telemetry granularity interact.
